headline: Reviewed proposed FY2028 budgets, including $420,000 for legal services and a $350,000 IT reserve contribution.
summary: Staff presented proposed FY2028 budgets for several departments, a day after they went to the Town Council. Human Resources proposed $357,245, up $29,835 from FY2027. Finance discussed replacing the New World software system, which faces a 2030 cloud migration deadline.
plain_text:
LONDONDERRY BUDGET COMMITTEE 
Draft Meeting Minutes – November 10th, 2026 
Meeting Minutes prepared by Matt Tapley 
Moose Hill Council Chambers, 268B Mammoth Road, Londonderry, NH 03053 
1. Attendance 
Present: 
• Kate Burbidge (Chair) 
• Isaac Fernandez (Member at Large) 
• Nicole Dery (Vice-Chair) 
• Matt Tapley (Secretary) 
• Andria Hansen (Member at Large) 
• Rebecca Roe (Member at Large) 
Absent: 
• Jeff Penta (Member at Large) 
• Shawn Faber (Town Council Liaison) 
Town Staff and Guests: 
• Kim Bernard (Acting Town Manager and Police Chief) 
• Kirsten Hildonen (Administrative Services Director) 
• Laura Keeley (Assistant Assessor) 
• Christine Wholley (Permit Technician) 
• Tara Koza (Human Resources Director) 
• Cherie Fuller (Human Resources Administrator) 
• Jacob LaFontaine (Planning and Economic Development Director) 
• Jeremy Spaulding (Cyber Services Director) 
• Justin Campo (Finance Director) 
• Sarah Jardim-Lee (Controller) 
2. Call to Order 
Chair Kate Burbidge called the meeting to order at 6:30 PM, and the Committee recited 
the Pledge of Allegiance. 
3. Public Comment 
Nicole Dery moved to open public comment. Rebecca Roe seconded. Chair Kate 
Burbidge opened public comment, and no one came forward. A motion was made to 
close public comment, and the Chair declared it closed. The Committee agreed 
unanimously to open and close public comment without formal votes. No public 
comment period was reopened at the end of the workshop.
The Chair noted that the meeting agenda had not been posted on the Town website and 
said an agenda would be posted for the next meeting. 
4. New Committee Business 
The Committee reviewed the proposed FY2028 department budgets presented to the 
Town Council the previous day. 
4.1 Administration 
• Kirsten Hildonen reported that the proposed Town Manager budget was 
approximately $160,000 below FY2027, largely because the prior deputy position’s 
salary was now budgeted in Planning and Economic Development. The proposed 
budget was $10,715 above default, primarily to allow for Town Manager salary 
adjustments. Administration discussed restoring the deputy or assistant position or 
providing a stipend, and outlined a possible internship estimated at $12,000 for three 
ten-week terms. 
• The Town Council budget was roughly level with FY2027. Higher legal-notice costs 
were partly offset by moving the $1,700 veterans breakfast contribution to General 
Government. The Committee’s own proposed budget rose from $1 to $621 for 
training and related travel. 
• General Assistance included an $18,000 direct-aid forecast, an $81,000 Community 
Health Services contract, and a $50,000 community services grant line. 
Administration requested a 5% grant increase for Council consideration. Cultural 
Affairs called for level funding for Old Home Day, fireworks and the Historical 
Society, higher Heritage Commission legal-notice costs, and a $3,500 reduction for 
the Arts Council based on sponsorship revenue. Conservation Commission funding 
was proposed at the existing level. 
• Administration proposed $420,000 for legal services, including $300,000 for general 
representation based on a three-year average of hours and an hourly rate that rose 
from $290 to $375. The forecast also covered litigation, the Auburn Road Superfund 
site, code enforcement and investigations. The Committee discussed prior 
underbudgeting, upcoming union negotiations, and the costs and tradeoffs of 
changing firms or hiring in-house counsel. Isaac Fernandez asked about the basis 
for the litigation estimates, who contacts outside counsel, and the Town’s experience 
with its attorneys. He also asked for a comparison with similarly sized towns. Staff 
said it could be explored. 
4.2 Assessing 
• Laura Keeley reported that the department was back to three staff and intended to 
catch up on cyclical property inspections. The 2027 revaluation drove higher printing 
and mailing costs for notices. Management services covered assessing software and 
contracted services. Whitney remained the Town’s assessing contractor.
• Matt Tapley asked whether the Town could consolidate printing orders to negotiate a 
discount. Staff distinguished commercial printing from newspaper legal notices and 
said the incoming procurement specialist would look for savings on recurring 
purchases. 
4.3 Building 
• The department reported a five-year average of approximately 2,288 permits and 
$871,000 in permit revenue annually. Approximately $34,000 of the proposed 
increase was attributed to contractual salaries and benefits. The proposal was below 
default. Permit Technician Christine Wholley explained that technical code books are 
purchased on a three-year cycle. 
4.4 Human Resources 
• Tara Koza presented a $357,245 proposal, up $29,835 from FY2027. Of the 
increase, $21,995 was attributable to salaries and benefits included in default and 
$7,840 to operating accounts. Changes included background checks, recruitment 
advertising, training and office supplies, partly offset by a $1,500 reduction in 
employee programs. Some costs, including $1,200 for toner, had been carried in 
other departments. 
• Koza reported that the Town workforce grew from 207 to 256 over ten years while 
HR was staffed by two people. She cited seasonal hiring, onboarding and 
compliance as workload drivers. She described a continuing need for an HR 
assistant and said the FY2028 proposal excluded the position. Chair Kate Burbidge 
asked about the ratio of HR staff to employees and the amount of spending 
transferred into the HR budget. 
4.5 Planning and Economic Development 
• Jacob LaFontaine reported that the director’s salary transfer from the Town Manager 
budget and other salary and benefit changes accounted for most of the increase. 
The department reported that its 400-foot abutter notification radius increased supply 
and postage costs, which it offsets through applicant fees. 
• The department was recruiting a town planner and working to accept land-use 
applications in OpenGov. Management services included support from the Southern 
New Hampshire Planning Commission for work beyond staff capacity. 
4.6 Cyber Services / Information Technology 
• Jeremy Spaulding presented a proposed budget of approximately $1.227 million, 
including about $92,000 for replacement equipment and a $40,000 estimate to 
expand access control to the Senior Center and Town Common. He reviewed line-
item transfers and estimated that phone and internet costs could rise by 
approximately $27,000 as contracts expire in March. He was evaluating lower-cost 
options.
• Spaulding discussed the workload of the two-person department and the priority 
given to equipment already failing or nearing failure, including Fire Department 
vehicle computers and ambulance modem kits. Isaac Fernandez asked how Cyber 
Services tracks Fire Department equipment due for replacement. Spaulding 
identified a roughly 20% annual equipment replacement cycle as a goal for FY2029 
planning. Police maintain a separate IT operation. 
4.7 Finance 
• Finance reported that the proposed budget was $40,995 above FY2027 and $150 
below default. Wage and audit fee increases were the main default-budget drivers. 
Finance described the new procurement role and discussed the possible placement 
of a grant writer within the department. 
• Finance discussed replacing the New World enterprise resource planning system. 
Staff reported a 2030 cloud migration deadline if the Town stays with New World, an 
anticipated annual charge of $84,111 and a 5% annual escalation. Members 
discussed the risk of paying for two migrations and the staff time spent on manual 
payroll, accounts payable and budget processes. 
• Staff said the proposed $350,000 contribution to the IT capital reserve fund would 
primarily support data migration and training. Controller Sarah Jardim-Lee reported 
that staff had contacted alternative vendors and were awaiting funding before 
scheduling detailed demonstrations. 
5. Liaison Reports 
• No liaison reports were recorded. 
6. Old Committee Business 
• No old committee business was recorded. 
7. Other Business 
7.1 Budget Workshop Process 
• The Chair discussed holding separate workshops for most departments and joint 
presentations with the Town Council for larger budgets. Members discussed inviting 
departments back when follow-up questions warranted a second appearance. Staff 
encouraged members to submit questions in advance and said the presentations 
would be posted before the next meeting. 
• In response to a question about health insurance, staff described a Town/employee 
premium split of at least 95/5 for bargaining units other than Police and Fire. 
8. Approval of Minutes 
• No approval of prior minutes was recorded.
9. Upcoming Meetings and Events 
Next meeting announced for Tuesday, November 17, 2026, at 6:30 PM. 
• The Committee planned to use that meeting to discuss which departments to invite 
back on December 1, and to revisit the need for the December 8 session on 
December 1. 
10. Adjournment 
Nicole Dery moved to adjourn. Rebecca Roe seconded. The Committee agreed 
unanimously to adjourn without a formal vote. The Chair declared the meeting adjourned 
at 8:15 PM.
